tier1.text: Each subclavian vein collects blood from the axillary vein, the main vein draining the arm. Each subclavian vein lies deep in the chest, starting where the axillary vein enters from the armpit. Each subclavian vein then joins veins from the head and neck to form a brachiocephalic vein. The subclavian veins are also where lymph, extra fluid drained from body tissues, flows back into the blood.

quotes.quote: On both the left and right sides, the subclavian vein forms when the axillary vein passes through the body wall from the axillary region. It fuses with the external and internal jugular veins from the head and neck to form the brachiocephalic vein.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

quotes.quote: brachiocephalic vein: one of a pair of veins that form from a fusion of the external and internal jugular veins and the subclavian vein
quotes.section: Chapter 20 Key Terms (The Cardiovascular System: Blood Vessels and Circulation)
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

quotes.quote: The surplus fluid in the interstitial space that is not returned directly back to the capillaries is drained from tissues by the lymphatic system, and then re-enters the vascular system at the subclavian veins.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

quotes.quote: Lymph is the term used to describe interstitial fluid once it has entered the lymphatic system.
